items.title: Split augmented simplicial schemes and matching objects
items.axiom_use: No selection is made in the definition; the axiom dependency is inherited from the cited finite-limit and coproduct constructions of schemes.
items.statement: Fix a base scheme $S$ and work in the category of $S$-schemes, in which finite limits and coproducts exist. An augmented simplicial $S$-scheme is a simplicial object in this category augmented over $S$, with face and degeneracy maps over $S$; its matching object $M_p(X_\bullet)=(\operatorname{cosk}_{p-1}\operatorname{sk}_{p-1}X_\bullet)_p$ is the limit of the boundary diagram of structure maps out of degrees below $p$, with $M_0(X_\bullet)=S$ and canonical boundary maps $X_p\to M_p(X_\bullet)$. Its $N$-construction adjoins to $X_p$ one copy of $X_q$ for each order-preserving surjection $[p]\twoheadrightarrow[q]$ with $q<p$, with multiplication given by the identity on $X_p$ and the degeneracies on the copies; the object is split when this multiplication is an isomorphism in every degree. An augmented simplicial object is a proper hypercover of $S$ when the augmentation $X_0\to S$ and all canonical boundary maps are proper and surjective. Neither smoothness nor properness of the individual terms is part of the definition.
items.strategy: Definition only, so no proof section. The vocabulary covers augmented simplicial schemes over an arbitrary base, matching objects as limits of boundary diagrams, the Deligne $N$-construction and splitness, and the proper hypercover condition; remarks record the nondegenerate-part decomposition, the closed-subscheme presentation of matching objects over a separated base and the extension data of SGA 4 V bis 5.1.3 without claiming their proofs here.

references.title: Pierre Deligne, Theorie de Hodge III, Publ. Math. IHES 44 (1974) 5-77, (6.2.1)-(6.2.4)
references.locator: (6.2.1)-(6.2.2) the N-construction and the definition of a split (scinde) simplicial object; (6.2.3)-(6.2.4) the matching-object extension data, citing SGA 4 V bis 5.1.3

items.title: Blowups of projective schemes are projective
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the Proj/Rees construction and from the eventual global generation of coherent twists; no other selection is made. The construction is otherwise explicit.
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be an integral projective complex scheme of finite type, with structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C$ ([[def-projective-morphism-pre-proj]]), and let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a nonzero finite-type quasi-coherent ideal sheaf ([[def-quasi-coherent-ideal-sheaf]]). Then the blowup $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X$ of [[def-blowup-scheme-along-ideal]] is projective over $\mathbb C$: for some $M\ge0$ its structure morphism factors as a closed immersion $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^M_{\mathbb C}$ followed by the projection. Consequently every composition of blowups of an integral projective complex scheme along nonzero finite-type ideal sheaves remains integral and projective over $\mathbb C$.
items.strategy: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Sources: The Stacks Project, Divisors, Section 31.33, Lemma 31.33.13 (a blowup in a finite type ideal sheaf is a projective morphism with relatively ample tautological sheaf; tag 01OF page read in full) and Ravi Vakil, Foundations of Algebraic Geometry (June 27, 2011 draft), 19.4 (the blowup resolves the indeterminacy of a rational map to projective space, pp. 391-394). [F1] [[cor-rational-map-to-projective-space-resolved-by-base-ideal-blowup]]: for an integral finite-type $k$-scheme $X$, an invertible $L$, and finitely many meromorphic sections $s_0,\dots,s_n$ of $L$ whose generated subsheaf is $F=\sum_i\mathcal O_Xs_i\subseteq L$, the fractional blowup $B=\operatorname{Proj}_X\bigoplus_{k\ge0}(F\otimes L^{-1})^k$ is integral and $(\pi,\psi):B\hookrightarrow X\times_k\mathbb P^n_k$ is the schematic closure of its graph; in particular a closed immersion. [F2] [[lem-eventual-global-generation-coherent-twists]]: on a scheme projective over a Noetherian ring with ample invertible $L$, every coherent sheaf becomes globally generated after twisting by a sufficiently high power of $L$. [F3] [[def-projective-morphism-pre-proj]], [[def-very-ample-invertible-sheaf-relative]], [[def-relatively-ample-invertible-sheaf]], [[lem-very-ample-implies-ample]]: a closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}$ exhibits $\mathcal O_X(1)=i^*\mathcal O(1)$ as H-very ample relative to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C$, hence ample on $X$. [F4] [[cor-segre-veronese-embedding]]: $\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}\times_{\mathbb C}\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}\to\mathbb P^M_{\mathbb C}$ is a closed embedding. [F5] [[lem-blowup-reduced-integral-under-domain-rees]]: blowing up an integral scheme in a nonzero finite-type ideal sheaf yields an integral scheme. Step 1.1 (twist and generate). Fix a closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}$ and put $L_0=\mathcal O_X(1)$; by [F3] $L_0$ is ample. Apply [F2] to the coherent sheaf $\mathcal I$ to obtain $d\ge1$ with $\mathcal I\otimes L_0^{\otimes d}$ globally generated; write $L=L_0^{\otimes d}$ and $F=\mathcal I\otimes L=\mathcal I(d)$. Choose finitely many global sections $s_0,\dots,s_n\in H^0(X,F)$ generating $F$ as an $\mathcal O_X$-module; viewed as meromorphic sections of $L$ they are not all zero because $\mathcal I\ne0$. Step 2.1 (the graph model is the blowup). By the displayed identity $F\otimes L^{-1}\cong\mathcal I\otimes L\otimes L^{-1}\cong\mathcal I$, so the fractional blowup ([[def-blowup-fractional-ideal]]) of [F1] is $B=\operatorname{Proj}_X\bigoplus_{k\ge0}\mathcal I^k=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X$, and [F1] provides a closed immersion $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X\hookrightarrow X\times_{\mathbb C}\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}$. Step 3.1 (projectivity of the graph model). The closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}$ base changes to a closed immersion $X\times_{\mathbb C}\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}\times_{\mathbb C}\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}$, and [F4] composes it with a closed embedding into $\mathbb P^M_{\mathbb C}$. Hence $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X$, identified with a closed subscheme of $X\times_{\mathbb C}\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}$, is a closed subscheme of $\mathbb P^M_{\mathbb C}$: its structure morphism is H-projective over $\mathbb C$ by [[def-projective-morphism-pre-proj]]. Step 4.1 (compositions). Induct: after the first blowup, [F5] keeps the source integral, and Step 1.1-3.1 applies again to the next nonzero finite-type ideal; the composite of finitely many H-projective morphisms over $\mathbb C$ is again a closed immersion into projective space by applying the same definition step by step. Empty centres give identity blowups and change nothing. This is the projectivity input used by the hyperresolution construction below on this page. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1]

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, Section 31.33 (Blowing up), Lemma 31.33.13

items.title: Smooth projective proper hyperresolutions
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from Chow's lemma, the embedded desingularization theorem and the Proj/Rees constructions. Finitely many choices of smooth projective covers and of common refinements are made from nonempty sets; each matching-object step selects one cover of a fixed proper scheme.
items.statement: Assume AC. Every proper complex algebraic variety $Y$ admits a split simplicial proper hypercover $a:Y_\bullet\to Y$ with every $Y_p$ smooth projective. Here proper hypercover means that $Y_0\to Y$ and each map $Y_p\to(\operatorname{cosk}_{p-1}Y_\bullet)_p$ is proper and surjective. Two such systems admit a third smooth projective proper hypercover mapping to both over $Y$. Every morphism between proper varieties can be lifted to a morphism between such hypercovers after refining the source. Degree-$n$ cohomology uses only the finite skeleton through degree $n+1$.
items.strategy: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Sources: Pierre Deligne, Theorie de Hodge III, (6.2.5)-(6.2.8) (inductive construction of proper split hypercovers, dominated common refinements and lifting of morphisms; printed pp. 19-21) and Andrzej Weber, Notes on Mixed Hodge Structures, (4.1.1)-(4.2.2) (hypercoverings as simplicial varieties, comparability; printed pp. 9-10). [F1] [[lem-chow-lemma-proper-noetherian]]: for every proper complex scheme $T$ there is a projective $T'$ and a proper surjective $T'\to T$ which is an isomorphism over a dense open. [F2] [[thm-weak-embedded-desingularization]]: a reduced closed subscheme $Y\subseteq\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}$ has an embedded desingularization whose strict transform $\widetilde Y$ is smooth, is a closed subscheme of a composition of blowups $X_r\to\dots\to\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}$ along regular centres, and maps to $Y$ properly, birationally on each irreducible component, isomorphically over the smooth locus. [F3] [[lem-blowups-of-projective-schemes-are-projective]] (whose statement already includes the composition clause): such a tower of blowups of $\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}$ stays integral and projective, so $\widetilde Y$, being closed in $X_r$, is smooth projective and $\widetilde Y\to Y$ is proper and surjective (its closed image contains the dense smooth locus of the reduced $Y$). [F4] [[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]], [[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]], [[def-proper-morphism]], [[lem-proper-stable-base-change]], [[lem-proper-stable-composition]] fix the simplicial, fibre-product and properness vocabulary: matching objects are finite limits of the previous terms; finite fibred products of proper morphisms are proper, and composites of proper morphisms are proper. Step 1.1 (smooth projective covers of projective reduced schemes). By [F2] and [F3], every reduced projective complex scheme $Z$ admits a smooth projective $\widetilde Z$ and a proper surjective morphism $\widetilde Z\to Z$ that is an isomorphism over the smooth locus. Step 2.1 (degree zero). Apply [F1] to $Y$ to get a projective $X'$ and a proper surjection $X'\to Y$; replacing $X'$ by its reduced structure (a closed immersion, hence proper and surjective onto $X'$) and applying Step 1.1 gives a smooth projective $Y_0$ and a proper surjection $Y_0\to Y$. Step 3.1 (inductive step and split structure). Suppose a split simplicial object through degree $p-1$, augmented over $Y$, has been built with each term smooth projective and with proper surjective matching maps. Its degree-$p$ matching object $M_p$ is the limit of the previous face diagram; as the target $Y$ is separated and the previous terms are projective, $M_p$ is a closed subscheme of the finite product $\prod_{i<p}Y_i$, hence is a proper complex scheme. Apply [F1] to $M_p$ and then Step 1.1 to the resulting projective scheme to obtain a smooth projective $N_p$ with a proper surjection $N_p\to M_p$. Set $Y_p=N_p\sqcup\coprod_{\alpha:[p]\twoheadrightarrow[q],\,q<p}Y_q$, the second summand indexed by the order-preserving surjections, with faces of $N_p$ given by the matching projections and the remaining faces and degeneracies determined by the unique factorization of an ordinal map as a surjection followed by an injection. These factorizations satisfy the simplicial identities, the summand $N_p$ makes the matching map $Y_p\to M_p$ proper and surjective, and the explicit summands indexed by surjections exhibit $Y_\bullet$ as split. Induction over $p$ builds $Y_\bullet\to Y$. Step 4.1 (refinements and lifting). Given two smooth projective proper hypercovers, form the product diagram over $Y$; its matching covers are fibred products of proper surjections, hence proper and surjective by [F4], so the same induction produces a third smooth projective proper hypercover mapping to both. Given $g:Y\to Z$ between proper varieties, build the source hypercover together with maps into the target hypercover degree by degree: at each stage impose the previously constructed faces and the proposed map to the target term, obtaining a relative matching object that is again a finite limit of proper schemes; its projection to the source matching object is surjective because the target is a hypercover, and a smooth projective cover of it is provided by [F1] and Step 1.1. Step 5.1 (finite skeleton). In the normalized cochain simple complex the terms of simplicial degree $p$ have total degree at least $p$ for nonnegative coefficient degrees, so $H^n$ and its differentials involve only simplicial degrees through $n+1$; the infinite construction is the compatible union of its finite stages. This supplies the geometric input for the proper-weight theorem below on this page. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1]

items.title: Borel-Moore homology by locally finite chains
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used in the definition or in the induced proper pushforward.
items.statement: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space and $R$ a commutative ring. A formal sum of continuous $k$-simplices is locally finite when every point of $X$ has a neighbourhood meeting only finitely many of the images of the simplices with nonzero coefficient; these sums form the locally finite chain complex, coefficientwise boundary included, and its homology is the Borel-Moore homology $H_k^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;R)$. Ordinary singular chains are the sums with finite support, and only proper continuous maps induce pushforwards on locally finite chains.
items.strategy: Definition only, so no proof section. The clauses fix local finiteness, the boundary complex, the containment of ordinary chains and the proper-pushforward functoriality used by the companion theorem; the agreement with ordinary homology for compact spaces is proved separately on this page.

references.title: Mark Goresky, Lecture Notes on Sheaves and Perverse Sheaves, version of June 26, 2026
references.locator: 5.3 (the Borel-Moore sheaf of chains as locally finite chains, with the paracompactness remark) and 11.2 (the dual construction, the realization by closed locally finite chains and pushforward along proper mappings)

items.title: Borel-Moore and ordinary homology agree for compact spaces
items.axiom_use: The proof is choice-free: local finiteness supplies an open cover by small neighbourhoods and compactness extracts a finite subcover, with no selection of points or simplices.
items.statement: For a compact Hausdorff space $X$ and a commutative ring $R$, the inclusion of the ordinary singular chain complex into the locally finite chain complex of [[def-borel-moore-homology]] is an isomorphism, so $H_k^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;R)\cong H_k^{\mathrm{sing}}(X;R)$ in every degree, naturally for continuous maps of compact Hausdorff spaces; in particular the class map of a proper complex algebraic variety may be computed in ordinary singular homology.
items.strategy: Direct: a finite chain is locally finite; conversely local finiteness gives an open cover by neighbourhoods meeting finitely many images, compactness extracts a finite subcover, and only finitely many simplices can then have nonzero coefficient. Naturality follows since continuous maps of compact spaces are proper.

references.title: Mark Goresky, Lecture Notes on Sheaves and Perverse Sheaves, version of June 26, 2026
references.locator: 5.3: for a paracompact (in particular a compact Hausdorff) space one restricts to sums that are locally finite, which on a compact space have finite support

items.title: Proper cohomology and functorial mixed Hodge weights
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the smooth projective hyperresolution, the constructible descent theorem, the compact Kahler comparison and the logarithmic mixed Hodge theorem. Dependent choice is used exactly once, for the subordinate partition of unity producing the continuous cutoffs in the metrization of $Y^{\mathrm{an}}$; it is supplied from AC by [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]. The remaining steps make no new arbitrary selections.
items.statement: Assume AC. The rational cohomology $H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$ of every proper complex algebraic variety has a functorial mixed Hodge structure with weights at most $n$. For a morphism $g:Y\to U$ with $Y$ proper and $U$ smooth quasiprojective, its pullback $H^n(U)\to H^n(Y)$ is a mixed Hodge morphism for the logarithmic structure on $U$. If $Y\to X$ is proper with $X$ smooth projective of dimension $d$, the proper homological class map $$H_i^{\mathrm{BM}}(Y,\mathbb Q)=H_i(Y,\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbb Q)(d)$$ is a mixed Hodge morphism after the indicated Tate twist. Its image, and consequently the untwisted image in $H^{2d-i}(X)$, is a pure Hodge substructure. No smoothness of $Y$ is assumed.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and a proper complex algebraic variety $Y$; morphisms $g:Y\to U$ to a smooth quasiprojective $U$ and $h:Y\to X$ to a smooth projective $X$ of dimension $d$ where these are named.

[F1] [[thm-proper-varieties-admit-smooth-projective-hyperresolutions]]: every proper complex variety $Y$ admits a split simplicial proper hypercover $a:Y_\bullet\to Y$ with all $Y_p$ smooth projective; two such hypercovers are dominated by a third smooth projective one; every morphism of proper varieties lifts to a morphism of such hypercovers after refining the source; and degree-$n$ cohomology uses only the skeleton through degree $n+1$.

[F2] [[thm-proper-hypercovers-compute-constructible-derived-cohomology]]: for a proper hypercover $X_\bullet\to X$ of finite-type complex varieties and a bounded-below constructible coefficient complex $F$ of lower bound $a$, the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism $F\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_pRa_{p*}a_p^*F$, giving $R\Gamma(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_pR\Gamma(X_p,a_p^*F)$ and a strongly convergent spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X_p,a_p^*F)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(X,F)$ whose diagonal $p+q=m$ is finite and determined by levels $p\le m-a+1$, and all refinements induce the same comparison. For the constant rational complex $F=\mathbb Q_X$ the lower bound is $a=0$ and the spectral sequence is first-quadrant.

[F3] [[lem-mixed-hodge-complexes-give-functorial-cohomology-and-simplicial-weights]] and [[def-cohomological-mixed-hodge-complex]]: part (ii) turns a cosimplicial system of weight-zero rational Hodge complexes concentrated in nonnegative bidegrees, with strict differentials and pure cohomology of weight $q$ in bidegree $(p,q)$, into a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex whose simple complex carries a mixed Hodge structure with $\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n\cong E_2^{n-q,q}$, so that all weights of $H^n$ are at most $n$ when only nonnegative cosimplicial degrees occur.

[F4] [[thm-compact-kahler-hodge-decomposition-via-elliptic-harmonic-forms]] and [[lem-smooth-projective-analytification-has-rational-kahler-polarization]]: a smooth projective complex scheme $Z$ of pure dimension has analytification $Z^{\mathrm{an}}$ a compact Hausdorff second-countable complex manifold carrying a Kähler form from any ample class, and $H^q(Z,\mathbb Q)$ is pure of weight $q$ with functorial rational structure and strict Hodge filtration; for a finite disjoint union of such schemes the statements hold componentwise and sum.

[F5] [[lem-morphisms-of-mixed-hodge-structures-are-strict]]: mixed Hodge morphisms are strict for both filtrations, their kernels, images and cokernels carry mixed Hodge structures, and a morphism from a structure of weights at least $n$ to a structure of weights at most $n$ has pure image of weight $n$.

[F6] [[lem-locally-contractible-metric-spaces-have-singular-constant-sheaf-cohomology]], [[thm-constructible-sheaves-admit-finite-stratified-triangulations-and-finite-local-cohomology]], [[lem-finite-simplicial-open-stars-have-explicit-conical-product-charts]], [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]], [[thm-a-compact-hausdorff-space-is-regular-and-normal]], [[cor-compact-hausdorff-partitions-of-unity]] and [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]: the analytic topology of a complex algebraic variety is fixed by the cited definition; the triangulation theorem provides finite compatible smooth Whitney refinements and triangulations of quasi-projective charts; open stars of simplices have explicit conical product charts and are contractible; a compact Hausdorff space is normal, has subordinate continuous partitions of unity under dependent choice — which the last item supplies from AC — and the metrization and sheaf-singular comparison then identify derived constant-sheaf cohomology with singular cohomology on every open subset.

[F7] [[thm-logarithmic-complex-constructs-smooth-open-mixed-hodge-structures]]: for smooth quasiprojective $U$ with an SNC smooth projective compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, the logarithmic de Rham complex with its pole-count weight filtration constructs a functorial rational mixed Hodge structure on $H^n(U,\mathbb Q)$ of weights at least $n$, independent of the compactification, with $W_nH^n(U,\mathbb Q)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(X,\mathbb Q)\to H^n(U,\mathbb Q))$. Its empty-boundary construction gives the exact functorial Godement global-section model of the holomorphic de Rham complex of a smooth projective variety, with the degree Hodge filtration and the constant-sheaf rational comparison; the proof derives differential strictness from Hodge-de Rham $E_1$ degeneration.

[F8] [[def-borel-moore-homology]], [[lem-borel-moore-homology-of-compact-spaces]], [[thm-poincare-duality-for-oriented-topological-manifolds]], [[cor-cohomology-over-a-field-is-dual-to-homology-over-that-field]] and [[prop-cap-product-naturality-and-projection-formula]]: locally finite chains define Borel-Moore homology, which agrees with ordinary singular homology for compact spaces; for compact spaces and field coefficients cohomology is dual to homology via the Kronecker pairing; and on a compact oriented $2d$-manifold cap product with the fundamental class is an isomorphism $H^{2d-i}\to H_i$ compatible with the cup product and the trace, whose class has Hodge type $(d,d)$.

[F9] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: the standing hypothesis, inherited from the hyperresolution, descent and logarithmic suppliers, and used exactly once as dependent choice for the partition of unity in [F6].

## Proof

1.1 (Actual cosimplicial Hodge complexes.) Choose the smooth projective proper hypercover $a:Y_\bullet\to Y$ of [F1]. Use the exact functorial Godement construction of [F7], applied on every $Y_p$, and put $K_{\mathbb Q}^{p,q}=\Gamma(Y_p,C^q(\mathbb Q_{Y_p}))$ and $K_{\mathbb C}^{p,q}=\bigoplus_{k+t=q}\Gamma(Y_p,C^t(\Omega^k_{Y_p}))$, for $p,q\ge0$, with $F^b$ given by $k\ge b$. These are the resolved global de Rham complexes, not the complex of global holomorphic forms. Godement pullback along each face is induced by pulling a germ collection at a point to the stalk over its image; the successive cokernels preserve these maps, so their composites obey the simplicial identities and preserve $F$. The constant inclusion $\mathbb Q\otimes\mathbb C\to\Omega^0$ gives the functorial rational comparison; on cohomology it is the scalar-extension comparison of [F4]. Exactness and acyclicity of the resolution show $H^q(K_{\mathbb C}^p)=H^q(Y_p;\mathbb C)$, with the holomorphic-degree image filtration, and $H^q(K_{\mathbb Q}^p)=H^q(Y_p;\mathbb Q)$. The compact Hodge theorem [F4] gives pure weight $q$ and Hodge-de Rham $E_1$ degeneration on each smooth projective component. The latter makes the actual internal differential $F$-strict: if $dx\in F^b$, degeneration lifts the leading lower-filtration class of $x$ to a cycle up to a higher-filtration term and a boundary; subtracting the cycle and boundary raises the preimage filtration without changing $dx$, and finite induction supplies a preimage in $F^b$, as in the strict correction of [F7]. Thus every level is an actual weight-zero rational Hodge complex. Each internal total diagonal is finite, and $F^{q+1}K^{p,q}=0$, so [F3] applies to its first-quadrant simple complex, giving the mixed Hodge structure and $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(Y_p;\mathbb Q)$, $E_2$ degeneration and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n(sK)=E_2^{n-q,q}$. The terms have $p=n-q\ge0$, so weights are at most $n$, and the finitely many terms on every total diagonal are finite-dimensional by [F4]. Descent [F2] identifies the rational simple cohomology naturally with $H^n(Y;\mathbb Q)$, carrying this structure. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F7, construct, algebra]

2.1 Identify the descended cohomology with ordinary singular cohomology of the analytic space $Y^{\mathrm{an}}$ [F6]. The space $Y^{\mathrm{an}}$ is compact: $Y_0\to Y$ is proper and surjective and $Y_0$ is smooth projective, so $Y_0^{\mathrm{an}}$ is compact by [F4] and its image under the continuous surjection $Y_0^{\mathrm{an}}\to Y^{\mathrm{an}}$ is all of the compact space $Y^{\mathrm{an}}$; it is Hausdorff and second-countable in the analytic topology [F6]. For the local contractibility hypothesis of [F6], cover $Y$ by finitely many affine charts, each quasi-projective, and apply the triangulation theorem and the conical-star lemma of [F6] chartwise: at a point in the relative interior of a retained simplex $\sigma$, its open star is a neighbourhood with chart $\operatorname{relint}|\sigma|\times c_{<1}(L)$ taking the point to $(p,\mathrm{apex})$. Shrink the first factor to convex open neighbourhoods of $p$ and the second to cones of radius $0<\epsilon<1$. Compactness of $L$ gives uniform radial neighbourhoods at the apex, so these products form a neighbourhood basis; each is contractible by straight-line contraction of the first factor and radial contraction of the cone. The same basis restricted to any open subset proves its local contractibility. Metrizability is obtained from the cutoffs of [F6]: compactness and normality give finitely many chart pieces and continuous cutoff functions equal to one on each piece and supported in its affine chart, the products of the cutoffs with the coordinate functions give a continuous injection of the compact space into Hausdorff Euclidean space, and the induced metric has the analytic topology. The sheaf-singular comparison of [F6] then identifies $H^n(Y^{\mathrm{an}},\mathbb Q_{\mathrm{const}})\cong H^n_{\mathrm{sing}}(Y^{\mathrm{an}};\mathbb Q)$, and the mixed Hodge structure of step 1.1 is carried to $H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$; the only choice used is the dependent choice for the partition of unity, supplied from AC by [F6]. [F6, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 Independence and functoriality. If $a':Y'_\bullet\to Y$ is a second split proper hypercover with smooth projective terms, [F1] supplies a third such hypercover dominating both; the two refinements give filtered comparison maps between the corresponding cosimplicial systems and hence morphisms of the mixed Hodge complexes of step 1.1, and by [F2] both simple complexes compute the constant-sheaf cohomology of $Y$, so the induced maps on $H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$ are the identity; strictness [F5] upgrades this to an isomorphism of mixed Hodge structures, so the structure is independent of the diagram. A morphism $g:Y\to Y'$ of proper varieties lifts, after refining the source hypercover, to a morphism of the chosen hypercovers [F1], pullback of holomorphic forms along it is a morphism of the cosimplicial mixed Hodge complexes compatible with the comparisons, and independence of the hypercovers makes the induced map $g^*:H^n(Y',\mathbb Q)\to H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$ well defined and compatible with identities and composition. [F1, F2, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct]

3.2 (The smooth-open clause and the actual total map.) Let $g:Y\to U$ and choose the logarithmic comparison model on $X\supset U$ from [F7]. Define its pullback into the simple complex of step 1.1 to be supported in cosimplicial degree zero, using $g_0=ga_0:Y_0\to U$. Pullback of a logarithmic form is regular on $Y_0$: a boundary equation pulls back to a nowhere-zero holomorphic function, whose $d\log$ is regular. Apply the functorial Godement resolutions to obtain the internal chain map into $K_{\mathbb C}^{0,*}$ preserving holomorphic degree. Its first alternating face differential is zero, since $g_0d_0=g_0d_1$ on $Y_1$, so this degree-zero-supported map is an actual chain map into the simple total complex; no map into every positive cosimplicial degree is being implicitly summed. On the rational side the natural pullback from $Rj_*\mathbb Q_U$ along $jg_0$, with the augmentation comparison, gives the same degree-zero-supported map, and it is compatible with the logarithmic meridian comparison up to the permitted filtered homotopies. For weight indices $a<0$ the source pole filtration is zero; for $a\ge0$ the target $L_a$ is the whole first-quadrant simple complex, so the map preserves weights. It preserves $F$ by form degree. Thus it is a morphism of the mixed Hodge complexes, and descent identifies its cohomology map with the actual rational pullback $g^*:H^n(U;\mathbb Q)\to H^n(Y;\mathbb Q)$. The functoriality clause of [F3] makes this a mixed Hodge morphism. [F2, F3, F7, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 The class map. Let $h:Y\to X$ be proper with $X$ smooth projective of dimension $d$, so $Y^{\mathrm{an}}$ and $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ are compact and the Borel-Moore homology of $Y$ agrees with ordinary singular homology by [F8]. Give $H_i(Y,\mathbb Q)$ the dual of the mixed Hodge structure on $H^i(Y,\mathbb Q)$. For the dual filtrations in [[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]], finite-dimensional linear algebra identifies $\operatorname{Gr}^W_a(H^*)$ with $(\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-a}H)^*$; annihilator Hodge filtrations negate each pure type $(p,q)$ to $(-p,-q)$, so these pieces are pure of weight $a$ and the dual is a mixed Hodge structure. Its weights are at least $-i$. Transposing a filtration-preserving map preserves the annihilator filtrations, so dual pullbacks are mixed Hodge morphisms. The pushforward $h_*:H_i(Y,\mathbb Q)\to H_i(X,\mathbb Q)$ is dual, under the Kronecker pairings of [F8], to the pullback $h^*:H^i(X,\mathbb Q)\to H^i(Y,\mathbb Q)$, which is a mixed Hodge morphism by step 3.1; hence $h_*$ is a mixed Hodge morphism for the dual structures. Poincare duality for the compact oriented manifold $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ and the compatibility of cap product with the cup product and the trace [F8] identify $H_i(X,\mathbb Q)\cong H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbb Q)(d)$ as pure Hodge structures of weight $-i$, the fundamental class having type $(d,d)$ so that the Tate twist removes the shift. Composing the pushforward with this identification, the class map $H_i^{\mathrm{BM}}(Y,\mathbb Q)=H_i(Y,\mathbb Q)\to H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbb Q)(d)$ is a mixed Hodge morphism from a structure of weights at least $-i$ to the pure structure of weight $-i$, so by [F5] its image is a pure Hodge substructure of weight $-i$; untwisting, the image in $H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbb Q)$ is a pure Hodge substructure of weight $2d-i$. No smoothness of $Y$ was used. [F5, F8, step 1.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Boundaries and Choice accounting. For $Y=\varnothing$ every group is zero with the trivial structure and all clauses are vacuous; the degree $n=0$ case has all weights equal to $0$, consistent with the bound; the reducible and mixed-dimensional case is handled componentwise in [F4]; and the case $Y=X$ with $d=\dim X$ reduces the class map to Poincare duality itself. The Axiom of Choice [F9] is inherited from [F1], [F2] and [F7], and is used exactly once more as dependent choice for the subordinate partition of unity in step 2.1, supplied by [F6]. [F1, F2, F6, F7, F9, given, cases: empty zero one degenerate endpoints] ∎

items.title: Weights control restriction images into proper varieties
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the logarithmic Hodge and proper-weight suppliers only; the strictness computation itself makes no selection.
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $U$ be smooth quasiprojective over $\mathbb C$, let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be any smooth projective compactification, and let $g:Y\to U$ be a morphism with $Y$ proper (possibly singular and reducible). Then, in every degree $n$, $$\operatorname{im}(H^n(X,\mathbb Q)\xrightarrow{(jg)^*}H^n(Y,\mathbb Q))=\operatorname{im}(H^n(U,\mathbb Q)\xrightarrow{g^*}H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)).$$ Both images are pure Hodge substructures of weight $n$. This includes the restriction of a smooth projective total space to a proper singular fibre through an open subvariety, which is the exact use in de Cataldo-Migliorini Proposition 8.3.2.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, a smooth quasiprojective $U$ with a smooth projective compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and a morphism $g:Y\to U$ with $Y$ proper.

[F1] [[thm-logarithmic-complex-constructs-smooth-open-mixed-hodge-structures]]: the logarithmic mixed Hodge structure on $H^n(U,\mathbb Q)$ has weights at least $n$ and satisfies $W_nH^n(U,\mathbb Q)=\operatorname{im}(j^*:H^n(X,\mathbb Q)\to H^n(U,\mathbb Q))$ for every smooth projective compactification, independently of the chosen $j$; for a non-SNC boundary the logarithmic theorem proves the same actual image formula by SNC domination and its modification-image supplier.

[F2] [[thm-proper-cohomology-has-functorial-mixed-hodge-weights-at-most-degree]]: the proper variety $Y$ carries a functorial mixed Hodge structure on each $H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$ with $W_nH^n(Y,\mathbb Q)=H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$, and the pullback $g^*:H^n(U)\to H^n(Y)$ for the actual morphism $g:Y\to U$ with proper $Y$ and smooth quasiprojective $U$ is a mixed Hodge morphism for the logarithmic structure on the source.

[F3] [[lem-morphisms-of-mixed-hodge-structures-are-strict]] and [[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]: a mixed Hodge morphism $f$ is $W$-strict, so $f(W_a)=f(H)\cap W_aK$ for every $a$; its image with the induced filtration is a mixed Hodge structure; and a morphism from a structure of weights at least $n$ to a structure of weights at most $n$ has pure image of weight $n$.

[F4] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: the standing hypothesis, inherited from the two cited theorems.

## Proof

1.1 By [F3] applied to the mixed Hodge morphism $g^*$ and the strictness identity $g^*(W_nH^n(U))=\operatorname{im}g^*\cap W_nH^n(Y)$, the target weight bound $W_nH^n(Y)=H^n(Y)$ of [F2] reduces the right-hand side to $\operatorname{im}g^*$; by [F1] the image of $W_nH^n(U)$ under $g^*$ is $g^*(\operatorname{im}j^*)=\operatorname{im}(g^*j^*)=\operatorname{im}((jg)^*)$. Hence the two asserted images agree as actual subspaces of $H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$, without choosing a splitting of the weight filtration on $H^n(U,\mathbb Q)$. [F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 Put $I=\operatorname{im}g^*$. Strictness gives $W_{n-1}I=g^*(W_{n-1}H^n(U))$, and by [F1] the source has weights at least $n$, so $W_{n-1}I=0$; the target bound gives $W_nI=I$. Hence the induced mixed Hodge structure on $I$ is pure of weight $n$, and by step 1.1 the image of $(jg)^*$ is the same pure substructure. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Boundaries and Choice accounting. If $U=\varnothing$ or $Y=\varnothing$ all groups vanish and the claim is vacuous; the degree $n=0$ case gives weight-zero images by the same strictness argument; the case $U=X$ has $j=\mathrm{id}$ and $W_nH^n(U)=H^n(U)$, so both images are the full image of $g^*$, consistent with the statement; and $Y$ smooth or reduced is not required, the target bound being the only hypothesis on the target. The Axiom of Choice [F4] is inherited from [F1] and [F2]; no selection is made in this argument. [F1, F2, F4, given, cases: empty zero one degenerate endpoints] ∎

items.title: A proper singular curve with weight-zero cohomology
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the proper mixed-Hodge and descent suppliers; the explicit Cech computation adds no selection.
items.statement:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). A rational projective curve with one ordinary node has one-dimensional
$H^1(C,\mathbb Q)$ of weight $0$, illustrating that proper singular cohomology
need not be pure of its degree.
items.strategy:
## Verification

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), a rational projective curve $C$ with one ordinary node, and its normalization $\nu:\mathbb P^1\to C$ identifying two distinct points $a,b$ and an isomorphism over the smooth locus.

[F1] [[cor-normalization-resolves-singularities-of-curves]] and [[cor-finite-morphism-proper]]: the normalization of an integral projective curve over a perfect field is a nonsingular projective curve and the normalization map is finite and birational, hence proper and surjective; for the rational nodal curve the normalization is $\mathbb P^1$ and $\nu$ is an isomorphism over the smooth locus.

[F2] [[thm-proper-hypercovers-compute-constructible-derived-cohomology]] and [[thm-proper-cohomology-has-functorial-mixed-hodge-weights-at-most-degree]]: the Cech nerve of a proper surjection is a proper hypercover, its descent spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(C_p,\mathbb Q)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(C,\mathbb Q)$ is strongly convergent with finite diagonals, and for a proper hypercover with smooth projective terms the associated mixed Hodge complex has $\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n(C,\mathbb Q)\cong E_2^{n-q,q}$ with weights at most $n$.

[F3] [[thm-stereographic-projection-riemann-sphere-homeomorphism]], [[cor-homology-of-spheres]] and [[cor-cohomology-over-a-field-is-dual-to-homology-over-that-field]]: $\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)\cong S^2$, so $H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$ and $H^1(\mathbb P^1,\mathbb Q)=0$, the latter as the dual of $H_1(S^2;\mathbb Q)=0$.

1.1 The Cech nerve $C_\bullet$ of the normalization has degree-$p$ term $C_p=\mathbb P^1_d\sqcup T_p$, where $T_p$ consists of the $2^{p+1}-2$ isolated points indexed by the nonconstant tuples in $\{a,b\}^{p+1}$: over the node the fibre product of copies of $\nu$ has one reduced point per tuple of preimages, and over the smooth locus it is the diagonal copy of $\mathbb P^1$ [F1]. Each $C_p$ is therefore a finite disjoint union of a smooth projective curve and reduced points, hence smooth projective, and the matching maps of the Cech nerve are base changes and finite products of the finite surjection $\nu$, hence proper and surjective, so $C_\bullet\to C$ is a proper hypercover to which [F2] applies. Taking cohomology gives $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(C_p,\mathbb Q)$, which vanishes for $q\ge1$ except in degree two where it is $\mathbb Q$ on the diagonal component; on the degree-zero row $E_1^{p,0}=H^0(C_p,\mathbb Q)$ is the direct sum of one copy of $\mathbb Q$ for the diagonal and one for each nonconstant tuple. [F1, F2, F3, construct, algebra]

2.1 Compute the degree-zero row in low degrees. On $C_0=\mathbb P^1$ one has $E_1^{0,0}=\mathbb Q$, and on $C_1=\mathbb P^1_d\sqcup\{ab\}\sqcup\{ba\}$ one has $E_1^{1,0}=\mathbb Q_d\oplus\mathbb Q_{ab}\oplus\mathbb Q_{ba}$; the alternating sum of the two face pullbacks $\delta^0$ sends a constant to the differences of the two diagonal values, hence is zero. On $C_2$ the six nonconstant tuples contribute the coordinates for $(aab),(aba),(abb),(baa),(bab),(bba)$, and evaluating the alternating sum $\delta^1(c)$ on these components and on the diagonal gives $c_d$ on $(aab),(abb),(baa),(bba)$ and $c_{ab}+c_{ba}$ on $(aba),(bab)$, where $c=(c_d,c_{ab},c_{ba})$. Hence $\delta^1(c)=0$ exactly when $c_d=0$ and $c_{ba}=-c_{ab}$, so $E_2^{1,0}=\ker\delta^1/\operatorname{im}\delta^0$ is one-dimensional, generated by $(0,1,-1)$. [step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The other total-degree-one entry is $E_1^{0,1}=H^1(\mathbb P^1,\mathbb Q)=0$ by [F3], so it contributes nothing; the spectral sequence is first-quadrant with finite diagonals and degenerates at $E_2$ by [F2]. Therefore $H^1(C,\mathbb Q)\cong E_2^{1,0}$ is one-dimensional, and by the weight identification of [F2] its graded pieces are $\operatorname{Gr}^W_0H^1=E_2^{1,0}=\mathbb Q$ and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_1H^1=E_2^{0,1}=0$. Since the weights of $H^1(C,\mathbb Q)$ are at most $1$, this forces $W_0H^1=H^1$: the whole one-dimensional space is pure of weight $0$ and type $(0,0)$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]), as asserted. [F2, step 2.1, algebra] ∎
